title: with power toys v0.100.2 it is not possible to assign different fancy zones to different "desktops" in Windows 11. Before it was working as expected

judgment.rationale: A commenter confirms the same behavior on 0.102.3101 and Windows 11 Insider: selecting a layout on one desktop forces it on all desktops. The current source has per-work-area and virtual-desktop layout state, but no runtime trace establishes why the per-desktop association is lost.
evidence: The original report says distinct layouts per Windows 11 desktop stopped working after version 0.100.2.
A later commenter says it still reproduces on 0.102.3101.0 with Windows 11 Insider build 26320.9876.
The latest commenter confirms that selecting a FancyZones layout on one desktop forces that same layout on all desktops.

Work-area configuration maps layouts to monitor/desktop work areas. Source at pinned main (237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c): https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/FancyZones/FancyZonesLib/WorkAreaConfiguration.cpp

AppZoneHistory receives a WorkAreaId that includes virtual-desktop identity. Source at pinned main (237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c): https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/237dc893c8c76b1bfa65994afda41ea7315a914c/src/modules/FancyZones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZonesData/AppZoneHistory.cpp

fix_assessment.rationale: The fix direction is grounded in a current report and the existing per-desktop work-area model; verify that state is being overwritten before changing persistence.

proposed_fixes.title: Keep FancyZones layouts scoped to virtual desktops
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: FancyZones is reusing or synchronizing layout state across virtual-desktop work areas instead of preserving the selected layout for each desktop.
plan: Trace the work-area and virtual-desktop identifiers used when selecting and restoring layouts on separate desktops.
If an update path writes the selected layout globally, preserve the per-desktop work-area association.
Add a regression with two virtual desktops, one monitor, and distinct custom layouts.
verification: Applying a layout on desktop A leaves desktop B's layout unchanged.
Switching repeatedly between desktops restores each desktop's assigned layout.

information_gaps.information: Whether changing the layout on desktop A changes desktop B immediately, before switching back to B, or only after returning to it.
information_gaps.why_needed: This distinguishes a shared selection update from an incorrect restore when switching virtual desktops.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: With different layouts assigned, change A and observe B without switching desktops; then switch to B and compare.

reproduce.title: Keep FancyZones layouts scoped to virtual desktops
prerequisites: Windows 11 with at least two virtual desktops and FancyZones enabled.
One monitor with two distinct custom layouts available.
setup: Assign layout A to desktop 1 and layout B to desktop 2.
steps: Switch to desktop 1 and verify layout A.
Switch to desktop 2 and verify layout B.
Change the selected layout on desktop 1, then switch to desktop 2 and check whether its layout changed too.
reproduce.expected_result: Each virtual desktop retains its own selected layout; changing one does not overwrite the other.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming this on 0.102.3101 and Windows 11 Insider. With distinct layouts assigned, could you change the selected layout on desktop A and check whether desktop B changes immediately while still on A, or only after switching back to B? This separates a shared layout update from a restore-time association issue.
